newsitem.title: UK: UK rates will be higher under new plan - Clarke.
newsitem.headline: UK rates will be higher under new plan - Clarke.

text.p: Former British Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said monetary policy would be tighter under the new arrangements announced on Tuesday by his successor Gordon Brown.

In an interview with BBC Radio Four, Clarke said he believed Brown would come to regret giving control over interest rates to a new monetary policy committee. "What you are going to see is, undoubtedly, tighter monetary policy than you might otherwise have got from a perfectly responsible Chancellor of the Exchequer who is prepared to take the broadest possible view of what is in the interests of British industry and commerce."
Clarke denied that he had made interest rate decisions on political grounds.
Rates peaked at 6.75 percent under his chancellorship but would have gone higher had Bank of England Governor Eddie George been setting rates, Clarke said, adding: "I was right not to go higher."
